name: Kozak Sequence Modulation
therapeuticGoalDescription: Increase or decrease protein synthesis by regulating mRNA translation without altering RNA abundance.
molecularDefect: Diseases in which the Kozak consensus context around the initiator AUG gives translation initiation efficiency that is too low or too high for therapeutic benefit.
suitableVariantTypes: Variants altering the Kozak consensus (gcc(A/G)ccAUGG); regulatory contexts where initiation efficiency limits protein output.
rnaTargetRegion: The Kozak consensus region immediately flanking the initiator AUG.
transcriptRequirement: Target transcript with an identifiable initiator AUG and flanking Kozak context.
asoChemistry: RNase H-independent steric-blocking ASOs: PMO, 2'-MOE full-phosphorothioate, LNA/DNA mixmers
designRules: Steric occupancy only - no RNase H recruitment. Effect size depends on surrounding nucleotide context; may require precise positioning relative to AUG.
advantages: Well-characterized consensus sequence (gcc(A/G)ccAUGG); predictable effect on initiation efficiency; works in both directions (strengthen or weaken).
limitations: Effect size depends on surrounding nucleotide context; may require precise positioning relative to AUG.
offTargetConsiderations: Kozak-like sequences exist in many transcripts; selectivity depends on flanking nucleotide identity.
clinicalTrialExamples: None identified; validated preclinically for globin, albumin, and other housekeeping genes.

evidenceLevel.note: Strong structural biology; validated in multiple systems; no approved therapy.

arbitration.note: Sub-mode of A2 (steric-blocking translation inhibition) but targeting the Kozak consensus specifically rather than general 5' UTR.
